messages.subject: using a "counter" that persists
parts:
I have a Shiny-server app that plots data sourced from an opendap server.  There are several dynamic and reactive selection inputs that change contextually to one another.  I also have an actionbutton whose intent is to only allow plotting when pressed.  This works great if just checking to see if it's value is greater than zero.  My thinking was that I could have a variable (lastCount) that I xould set to the value of the actionButton after a plot is done and then check this to ensure the reactive inputs do not force a replot.  Is there a way to keep a count that will not reset to zero every time.  I've tried to use reactiveValues, but that just sets off firing constantly.  If there is an example out there I could look at please pass it on.

- Dirk

messages.author: 5712068fdf482d27
messages.subject: Re: using a "counter" that persists
parts:
See if I understand you correctly. You seem to be suggesting that you are using something like if(input$myActionButton > 0) { .... do things ....}
therefore once it's been pressed ... do things ... will always be run whenever things inside the {} changes?

Have you considered do this

 if(input$myActionButton > 0) {
isolate({
 .... do things ....
})
}

or this

if(input$myActionButton == 0) return()
isolate({
.... do things ....
})

Now the ... do thing... part will only get executed if the button is pressed.
